My fields are small, only 4.5 mu, but I have farmed this wheat-maize rotation for 25 years so I know what works. My wife and I do most of the work ourselves. My son sends money sometimes, but I still count every yuan when I buy fertilizer.

For wheat, I plant in early October after the maize comes off. I buy the improved seed from the agro-shop in town — everyone on my lane uses the same variety, "Jimai" something, and it gives around 450-500 jin per mu if the weather is kind. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer — two bags per mu, that is about 50 kg of 15-15-15. Then I use rotary tiller service, 40 yuan per mu. In spring when the wheat stands up at jointing, I topdress one bag of urea per mu, about 20 kg. That puts my nitrogen around 17-18 kg per mu total. A little extra is better than too little — if the wheat turns yellow, I lose more than the cost of one bag.

For irrigation, I use the well. Wheat needs winter water before freeze, then jointing water, then grain-filling water — three times. My neighbor Old Wang sometimes skips the third one but last year his grain was shriveled, so I will not skip. Pesticide I spray twice — once for aphids and mites in April, once for rust and head blight at heading.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June, no tillage, just drill into the stubble. This saves labor and water. I use hybrid seed, the dealer says "Zhengdan" type. I put one bag of compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, then topdress urea at big-bellyball stage, about 15 kg. Maize I water once or twice depending on rain. Summer rain is usually enough. Pesticide twice — for corn borer and armyworm. Yield maybe 500-550 jin per mu.
